{
  "subtype": "causal_attribution",
  "outcome_variable": "product_score_outcome",
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "sentiment", "causal_role": "mediator", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Review sentiment is largely an expression/consequence of the reviewer's score experience, sitting on the path between the review content and the numeric score rather than being a common cause; treating it as a driver of score risks reverse-causation/mediation."},
    {"name": "product_avg_score", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Product-level baseline quality plausibly causes both which review attributes are present (treatment) and the individual score (outcome), acting as a common cause; not named in the query."},
    {"name": "score_vs_product_avg", "causal_role": "outcome", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "This is a re-centered version of the score itself (Score minus product_avg_score); it is essentially the outcome, not a treatment or confounder."},
    {"name": "helpfulness_ratio", "causal_role": "collider", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Helpfulness votes are caused by both review content and score/perception; it is a downstream effect (collider), and conditioning on it would induce bias rather than remove it."},
    {"name": "review_length", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Engagement/effort proxy that could jointly influence both the review's expressed attributes (treatment) and the score given (outcome); weakly plausible common cause, not named in query."},
    {"name": "flag_quality", "causal_role": "treatment", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "A candidate actionable cause: whether the review raises product-quality issues, whose effect on score is the attribution target ('actions that could improve product scores')."},
    {"name": "flag_taste", "causal_role": "treatment", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Candidate cause capturing taste-related mentions; an actionable attribute whose effect on score can be estimated."},
    {"name": "flag_misleading", "causal_role": "treatment", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Candidate cause: mentions of misleading description, an actionable driver of score."},
    {"name": "flag_shipping", "causal_role": "treatment", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Candidate cause: shipping-related complaints, an actionable driver of score."},
    {"name": "flag_value", "causal_role": "treatment", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Candidate cause: value/price mentions, an actionable driver of score."}
  ],
  "treatment_present": true,
  "treatment_columns": ["flag_quality", "flag_taste", "flag_misleading", "flag_shipping", "flag_value"],
  "confounders": [
    {"name": "product_avg_score", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.6},
    {"name": "review_length", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.35}
  ],
  "confounder_quality": 0.4,
  "rationale": "The system supplies a clear TREATMENT set: multiple thematic flags (quality, taste, misleading, shipping, value) that operationalise actionable candidate causes of the product score, satisfying requirement (a). Requirement (b) is only weakly met. product_avg_score is a genuine, query-surfaced common cause of both which review themes appear and the individual score, giving some real confounder evidence. review_length is a weaker candidate common cause. However, several added columns are NOT valid confounders: sentiment is a mediator/reverse-caused expression of the score, score_vs_product_avg is essentially the outcome itself, and helpfulness_ratio is a downstream collider whose adjustment would bias the estimate. So the causal setup has treatments plus one solid non-query confounder, but is diluted by mediators/colliders mislabelable as adjustments, yielding modest confounder quality."
}
